thread:
elaine: FYI customer on prod reported streaming response cut halfway and client auto-retries got charged twice. they pasted a truncated transcript and 2x tokens billed.

ingrid: ugh. any request ids, sample client logs, or curl repro?

elaine: let me paste the client log (sanitized). they do SSE with bearer token that rotates every 45s, long running chat ~3-4m. logs show: 
```
[2025-09-02T15:12:01Z] recv: data: <partial chunk...>
[2025-09-02T15:12:42Z] connection reset
[2025-09-02T15:12:43Z] retrying with fresh token -> 401
[2025-09-02T15:12:44Z] retry success -> new stream (duplicate billing)
```

elaine: customer uses ALB in front of our origin + Cloudflare as CDN. they mentioned ALB idle timeout is 60s default.

mike_sre: quick thoughts: token rotation during idle/half-close might leave client mid-KV-cache state so on reconnect it starts fresh and bills again. ALB half-close behavior can cause origin to see FIN then a new connection w/ new auth -> auth fails until token is propagated. also cloudflare sometimes coalesces very small SSE chunks when gzip/edge compression is on which can produce delayed 'last chunk' visible to client.

ingrid: can you share a minimal curl repro we can ask the customer to run? if we can reproduce with curl + short token TTL we can bisect ALB vs CF vs origin.

elaine: here's the simplified repro they ran: 
```
# simulate short token TTL by curling twice with different tokens
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer TOK_A" https://api.example.com/v1/chat/stream?model=redwood-beta
# wait 50s (simulate idle)
# then curl again with TOK_B (rotated token)
```

mike_sre: try this variant that uses netcat to keep the connection open and then triggers rotate: 
```
# start one stream
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer TOK_A" https://api.example.com/v1/chat/stream?model=redwood-beta &
# sleep 45
# rotate token on client and open new stream
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer TOK_B" https://api.example.com/v1/chat/stream?model=redwood-beta
```

elaine: customer also captured ALB access logs: last request shows 200 then client-side reset after 41s. no 499 from ALB though.

mike_sre: hmmm 41s -> shorter than ALB default 60s. could be client TCP/TLS keepalive or Cloudflare idle probes. can we get origin request logs with x-request-id?

elaine: attached origin trace id: r-id=03f2c9. forwarded to eng-runtime.

deploy-bot: deployment redwood/runtime@v3.14.2 rolled out to us-east-1 (15:09 UTC) :rocket:

tim_eng_runtime: taking a look. PoC hypothesis: when ALB sends FIN because it thinks connection idle, origin may still have queued tokens in kernel -> half-close semantics differ across LB types. NLB will do pass-through TCP and keep TLS, ALB terminates and can coalesce upstream events. combined with Cloudflare's response buffering + gzip, the SSE keepalive heartbeats might be swallowed. if client token rotates during that micro-window the reconnect handshake fails with 401 (we treat new token as fresh session).

cloudflare-eng: quick note from edge: if 'enable HTTP/2 to origin' + 'response buffering' are both on, small SSE frames can be merged into larger tcp segments and delayed until a flush threshold. this can look like a silent pause to clients. we see this especially with chunk sizes < 256B and gzip enabled.

ingrid: mitigation suggestions to pass to customer: 
- set ALB idle timeout > expected token rotation window (e.g. 300s) or align token TTL to be longer than ALB idle timeout
- disable Cloudflare response buffering for SSE routes (page rules / bypass cache / origin buffer off)
- ensure token refresh strategy avoids mid-stream rotation (use refresh token + fetch header-only renewal)
- enable our Resume-on-reconnect policy on their account (dedupe billing for quick reconnects < 5s) - will waive duplicate token billing for now as a short-term fix

tim_eng_runtime: we'll add a safeguard in the runtime: if reconnect occurs within 5s with a different token and same session fingerprint we can attempt KV-cache resume and not bill double. filing ENG-RUNTIME-872.

elaine: customer asked for prioritized fix; they hit a billing spike. I think we should offer credit and provide step-by-step mitigation.

tim_eng_runtime: agreed. I'll triage ENG-RUNTIME-872 and mark P1 for potential rollback if regression is found. in the meantime: support can propose the config changes + temporary credit.

ingrid: I'll draft the support email with repro steps, suggested ALB/CF changes, and offer for billing credit. :+1:

elaine: thanks all. assigning follow-up to @tim_eng_runtime and I'll keep customer looped. :eyes:
